what: `blaze check --fix` wrote `    #[blaze::nopanic]` and then the function at column 0 for every method with no doc comment above it (331 in bstd), and I committed the first two passes before reading a raw hunk: my summary of the diff stripped leading whitespace, so the damage showed as identical removed and added lines.
cost: a repair script, a lint fix and one more round of the shared build
cause: a function is linted by its body's anchor, whose text starts at the function, so the line's indentation is not in the text the fix reads (`Cx::text`); nothing formats or checks the layout of what `--fix` writes
workaround: the fix reads the closing brace's line when the function starts the text (commit on bstd-builds-1112); bstd reindented by script
fix: `BodySyntax` says its anchor's column (and compares it), so every fix that writes a new line can indent it; `--fix` runs `blaze fmt` on the lines it wrote, or the what-if refuses a suggestion that leaves a file unformatted where it was formatted
state: open: the lint is fixed, the anchor's column is not there
